raw.assessment: The incumbent preserves the specified product and rearrangeability, but its 11-minute median exceeds the target (D2-O2). Five reported partition errors suggest a contents problem without establishing five verified packing failures (D2-O3); seven of ten unaided arrangements expose a separate usability concern (D2-O4). Repeated simple layouts taking seven to nine minutes, with every extreme delay occurring in mixed batches, supports investigating configuration handling, but layout complexity is a confound (D2-O6). A concrete limit on a width-only insertion explanation is overlapping widths between first-attempt and retry parts (D2-O5); width interactions remain possible. These synthetic observations do not establish any proposed cause or successful remedy.

openings.claim: Selecting and checking a complete order-specific parts kit before insertion may reduce configuration-handling delays and partition errors.
openings.delta: Replace repeated shared-bin retrieval during assembly with a reusable staging tray and an order-specific component checklist.
openings.prediction: For matched layouts, staged kits reduce total selection-plus-checking time and discrepancies; unchanged insertion time would localize the benefit. No total-time improvement would undermine the proposed throughput benefit.
openings.probe: Reuse sample parts in counterbalanced trials with both workers, preserving layout mix, rare colors and mixed order sequence. Compare current handling with staged kits; separately time selection, insertion, checking and packing, including kit preparation. Independently inventory finished packages. Check setup cost, recurring cost and schedule before adoption.
assumptions: Reusable trays fit the single bench.
Preparation and checking overhead can fit the budget and delivery date.

openings.claim: With contents independently verified, does an order-specific placement diagram resolve short-partition uncertainty?
openings.delta: Discriminate instruction ambiguity from contents errors and persistent physical placement difficulty.
openings.prediction: Improvement with the tailored diagram supports an instruction contribution; persistent hesitation or insertion failures despite correct placement identification points toward another barrier.
openings.probe: Assign ten participants to current or tailored diagrams with matched verified organizers. Record unaided arrangement, short-partition placement decisions and insertion failures. Retain original parts, capacity, footprint, colors and removable joints; price a replacement diagram. Treat this small comparison as diagnostic, then assess all pilot success measures.
assumptions: Diagram preparation and printing fit the cost and schedule limits.

raw.assessment: Generic guidance and shared shape bins could generate interpretation and checking demand. Neither causal pathway is established. Missing-part reports do not distinguish shortages from interpretation errors; pilot success remains unproven.

openings.claim: The three-layout diagram may prompt unnecessary rearrangement of correctly supplied parts, creating uncertainty about the short partition and demand for help or replacement.
openings.delta: Feedback edge: generic guidance -> perceived arrangement discrepancy -> support demand. Substitute an order-specific initial-layout diagram on the existing sheet, retaining rearrangement guidance.
openings.prediction: With verified identical contents, order-specific guidance should reduce short-partition questions and perceived shortages. Persistent difficulty would weaken this hypothesis and favor investigating physical placement ambiguity.
openings.probe: Randomly assign ten participants to current or order-specific guidance, balancing ordered layouts where possible. Audit contents beforehand; record unaided success, short-partition questions and claimed shortages. This small comparison screens the mechanism; it cannot establish the 90% target.
assumptions: Replacement artwork uses the existing sheet within the cost cap.
Geometry, removability, assortment, ordered counts, colors and delivery date remain fixed.
Interpretation errors among shortage reports are possible but unestablished.

openings.claim: Shared shape bins may require repeated reconstruction of each order across locations; mixed layouts then generate rechecking and coordination demand that the storage arrangement perpetuates.
openings.delta: Feedback edge: shape-based organization -> repeated order reconstruction -> checking demand. Compare temporary order-specific kits made from the same bins.
openings.prediction: For matched mixed-layout work, kits should reduce return trips, selection corrections and total labor including kit preparation. Improvement confined to insertion would weaken this mechanism.
openings.probe: Use reusable spare-board trays in alternating matched trials with both workers. Separately record preparation, selection, checking, insertion and packing; audit contents. Count combined worker-minutes and elapsed order time so preparation and waiting remain visible.
assumptions: Kits preserve the product and every accepted layout and color.
Reusable trays fit the bench and initial budget without recurring material additions.
Trials and rollout fit the fixed delivery schedule; time savings are unproven.

openings.claim: Order kits/checklists may reduce reconstruction, retrieval, coordination, rechecking and contents errors.
openings.discriminator: Fewer trips/corrections and lower total labor support handling benefits; insertion-only gains weaken that mechanism; unchanged total time undermines throughput.
openings.fit: Product, removability and ordered counts/colors preserved; bench, budget and schedule fit unverified.
openings.probe: Counterbalance matched mixed-layout trials across both workers, including rare colors. Time preparation, selection, checking, insertion and packing; measure combined worker-minutes and elapsed time; independently audit packages.
openings.uncertainty: Complexity confounds delays; preparation/waiting may erase savings; reports do not prove packing failures.

openings.claim: Order-specific diagrams may reduce unnecessary rearrangement, short-partition confusion, perceived shortages and support demand.
openings.discriminator: Gains with verified identical contents support instruction effects; persistent difficulty despite correct placement identification suggests physical barriers.
openings.fit: Retain geometry, assortment, removable joints, ordered counts/colors and rearrangement guidance; price replacement artwork/printing.
openings.probe: Randomly assign ten participants to current/tailored guidance, balancing matched layouts. Audit contents; record unaided success, placement decisions, questions, claimed shortages and insertion failures.
openings.uncertainty: Interpretation-driven shortages unestablished; overlapping widths weaken width-only explanations but allow interactions; small trial is diagnostic.

lineage.reason: With A2; checklist and audits retained.
With Z1; reconstruction/coordination and labor retained.

post_distill.decision: Probe with reusable spare-board trays/sample parts. Before adoption verify 30x20 footprint/capacity, <=500 setup, <=0.40 recurring and fixed delivery. Synthetic evidence establishes no remedy; assess the 60-unit pilot against completeness >=98%, median time <=8 minutes and unaided success >=90%.
